@@ -0,0 +1,46 @@
+---
+assignees:
+- claude-code
+depends_on:
+- 01M1Y5GD85944ACE2XS6SA5XWJ
+- 01M1Y5JDJC7CHCDVFT92HD90TH
+position_column: todo
+position_ordinal: fffa80
+title: Correct the validator documents that still name swiftformat
+---
+## What
+
+Three validator documents state the old tool policy in words. After the gate moves, each states something that is not true. Correct them. Do the tasks "Move idioms-swift to the toolchain swift format" and "Rebalance the Swift prompt rules for the toolchain gate" first, because this task records what those two decided.
+
+Files to change:
+- `builtin/validators/swift/VALIDATOR.md`
+- `builtin/validators/swift/rules/access-control.md`
+- `builtin/validators/code-hygiene/VALIDATOR.md`
+- `crates/swissarmyhammer-validators/src/review/tool_rules/tests/shipped/swift_judgment_rules.rs`
+- `crates/swissarmyhammer-validators/src/review/tool_rules/tests.rs`
+
+`builtin/validators/swift/VALIDATOR.md` states this today:
+
+> Two tool rules of `builtin/validators/code-hygiene/` carry the deterministic half: `idioms-swift` runs swiftformat over every changed Swift file, and `disallowed-constructs-swift` runs swiftlint.
+
+Write instead that `idioms-swift` and `missing-docs-swift` run the toolchain's `swift format`, and that `disallowed-constructs-swift` runs swiftlint. Keep the rule that divides the two sets, because it does not change: **if a tool can decide it, the tool owns it.**
+
+The same file says formatting concerns belong to `swift-format`. That sentence is correct and becomes clearer, because `swift format` is now the one tool. Make the spelling the same everywhere: the command is `swift format`.
+
+Read `builtin/validators/swift/rules/access-control.md` and `builtin/validators/code-hygiene/VALIDATOR.md` for the same statements, and correct each one.
+
+Do not change any rule that this move does not touch.
+
+## Acceptance Criteria
+- [ ] `rg swiftformat builtin/` finds nothing outside a sentence that states the history on purpose.
+- [ ] `builtin/validators/swift/VALIDATOR.md` names the correct tool for each of the shipped Swift tool rules.
+- [ ] The spelling `swift format` is the same in every document.
+- [ ] Every document states which tool owns which bullet, and the statement agrees with the shipped rule files.
+
+## Tests
+- [ ] Write a test that reads every file under `builtin/validators/swift/` and `builtin/validators/code-hygiene/` and holds each to naming `swiftformat` nowhere.
+- [ ] Update `crates/swissarmyhammer-validators/src/review/tool_rules/tests/shipped/swift_judgment_rules.rs` and `crates/swissarmyhammer-validators/src/review/tool_rules/tests.rs` for the new tool names.
+- [ ] Run `cargo test -p swissarmyhammer-validators`. Every test passes.
+
+## Workflow
+- Use `/tdd` — write the failing tests first, then write the code that makes them pass. #swift
\ No newline at end of file
